The answer shapes the build: the work is pipeline and lakehouse engineering — modeled once, certified once, reused everywhere the decision appears.

First, the ground Data & Lakehouse work stands on in Care Management & Population Health: Care management succeeds on precision targeting and timely intervention: identifying rising-risk members, coordinating across providers, and proving quality outcomes. It is a data-discipline business — and the data discipline is usually the missing part.
What program matching crude costs is usually known only as a feeling. Turning that feeling into a signed number is the opening move; the engineering follows the evidence, never the other way round.
In Care Management & Population Health, the queues and waits that come up first:

items: Members matched to programs by blunt rules; engagement economics unmeasured.
Claims, clinical, SDOH and engagement data siloed; risk stratification runs on claims only.
HEDIS-class measures assembled manually per cycle; evidence assembled under deadline.
Care outreach, scheduling and follow-up run on call lists; gaps between contacts lose members.
